out: The Palestinian Authority has officially become the 123rd member of the International Criminal Court, granting the court jurisdiction over alleged crimes in Palestinian territories. This accession follows the signing of the Rome Statute in January and paves the way for potential investigations into war crimes.

A stray dog in Washington State survived being hit by a car, struck with a hammer, and buried in a field. After appearing to die, the dog managed to stagger to a nearby farm where she was found and rescued. She is now receiving care at a veterinary hospital and has been named Theia.

Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif has received a hero's welcome in Iran following high-stakes nuclear negotiations with U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry. Known for his polished and jovial demeanor, Zarif is working to finalize a breakthrough deal that could potentially end sanctions against Iran.

Five American clinicians who were monitored in Omaha after being exposed to Ebola in West Africa have been released from the hospital. None of the individuals developed the virus, and they were monitored following contact with a colleague who was diagnosed with the disease.

A Duke University student has admitted to hanging a noose near a student union, resulting in their removal from campus and an upcoming conduct review. While criminal investigations into the incident are ongoing, university officials are working to determine if anyone else was involved. In response to the act, students and faculty held a march to express solidarity and strength.

Trey Moses, a star high school basketball recruit, surprised his classmate Ellie Meredith by asking her to be his prom date. Although they come from different backgrounds, Trey chose to invite Ellie because of her great personality and easygoing nature.

Amnesty International's annual report alleges that governments are increasingly using the threat of terrorism to justify executions and advance the death penalty. The organization criticizes this trend as a shameful attempt to quell instability through the ill-conceived premise of deterrence.

Andrew Getty, a 47-year-old heir to the Getty oil fortune, has died of what appears to be natural causes. The Los Angeles Police Department stated there is no foul play involved and no criminal investigation is underway. An autopsy will be conducted to further investigate his death, which follows a history of several health issues.

As tropical storm Maysak (known locally as Chedeng) approaches the Philippines, authorities are warning citizens to prepare for potential flash floods and landslides. Although the storm has weakened from super typhoon status, it still maintains dangerous winds, prompting officials to preemptively ban outdoor activities like swimming and boating.

For the first time in eight years, legendary host Bob Barker made a special guest appearance on "The Price Is Right." At 91 years old, Barker returned to the show to host a classic game before handing the reins back to current host Drew Carey.

A 19-year-old British national, Yahya Rashid, has been charged with terror offenses following his arrest at Luton airport upon returning from Turkey. He faces charges related to preparing for acts of terrorism and intending to assist others in committing such acts. Rashid is scheduled to appear in court this Wednesday.

The release of *Furious 7* provides an opportunity for fans to honor the memory of Paul Walker, who died in a car crash in 2013. Those who knew him remember him as a man of great integrity and compassion, especially given his connection to the film franchise.

New research from the Anne Frank House suggests that Anne and Margot Frank died at least a month earlier than the previously recorded date of March 31, 1945. By re-examining survivor testimonies and historical archives, researchers concluded that the sisters likely did not survive to see the liberation of the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

A year after reports surfaced regarding his ties to the Koch brothers, Indiana Governor Mike Pence is facing intense backlash for signing a controversial religious freedom law. The legislation, which critics say allows for discrimination against the LGBTQ+ community, has drawn heat from business leaders and political observers alike.

The article discusses the high stakes and potential for public backlash when famous performers deliver the American national anthem. Using Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil as a recent example, it highlights how a poor performance can lead to being labeled a national disgrace.

Walmart's strong opposition to proposed religious freedom laws in several states has drawn significant attention, signaling growing support for LGBTQ+ rights within the American heartland. This stance, alongside recent decisions to increase employee wages, positions the retail giant as a bellwether for national social and economic trends.

In May 2014, Chinese authorities held a mass public sentencing in the Xinjiang region where 55 individuals were found guilty of various offenses following a series of violent attacks. The event, attended by thousands of spectators and guarded by armed soldiers, resulted in several prison sentences and three death penalties. This public trial was part of the government's "Strike Hard" campaign aimed at combating perceived terrorism and separatism in the region.

The French prosecutor investigating the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has denied reports that video footage from inside the plane has been recovered. While two magazines claimed a cell phone video of the final moments was found at the wreckage site, prosecutor Brice Robin stated that no such videos have been used in the investigation so far.

The Rev. Robert H. Schuller, founder of the "Hour of Power" ministry and the Crystal Cathedral megachurch, has died at the age of 88. He passed away peacefully following a battle with esophageal cancer.

Former Representative Michele Bachmann compared President Obama to Andreas Lubitz, the co-pilot accused of deliberately crashing a Germanwings flight. In a Facebook post, she argued that Obama's Iran deal is a dangerous move that will lead the nation to disaster.

After drifting at sea for over two months, 37-year-old Louis Jordan was rescued by the crew of the container ship *Houston Express*. Jordan had been lost since leaving South Carolina to fish, and his battered sailboat was initially mistaken for an abandoned wreck.

The United States and its partners reached a framework agreement with Iran in Switzerland designed to effectively prevent the country from building a nuclear weapon. Despite the deal's potential, significant political pushback is expected from lawmakers who have previously attempted to block such negotiations. The resulting debate is expected to be highly contentious as various political factions react to the announcement.

The historic California drought is a national concern because the state produces a significant portion of the country's fruits, vegetables, and nuts. As the drought enters its fourth year, Governor Jerry Brown has mandated a 25% cutback in water consumption to combat the crisis. Experts warn that these water shortages could lead to rising grocery prices for consumers across the nation.

The FBI has charged 30-year-old Keonna Thomas with attempting to travel overseas to fight for ISIS. Investigators cited numerous social media messages expressing her desire to join the terrorist group as evidence of her intent.

Since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been largely barred from attending men's sporting events, but officials announced that this ban will soon be lifted for certain matches. The new plan aims to allow women and families into stadiums, specifically targeting indoor sports events over the coming year. However, it remains unclear exactly which games will be eligible, as officials noted that restrictions may remain for certain male-centric sports.

Online activity has emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional mainstream media, particularly in authoritarian countries where access to print and broadcast outlets is limited. While the low cost of digital platforms makes them an attractive path for dissent, users still face various legal and social forms of resistance.

After months of speculation regarding her disappearance from the music scene, Avril Lavigne has revealed that she was battling Lyme disease. The singer explained that she was bedridden for five months with severe symptoms, including difficulty breathing and moving.

This article highlights a collection of the week's best videos, including a tour of former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson's abandoned Ohio mansion. The once-gaudy estate, which featured luxury amenities like a gold Jacuzzi, is set to be converted into a church.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the recent nuclear deal with Iran, arguing that it is a poor agreement and that a better alternative exists. He suggested that instead of choosing between this deal or war, world powers should maintain pressure on Iran to secure more favorable terms.

The owners of Memories Pizza in Walkerton, Indiana, faced significant backlash after stating they would refuse to cater weddings for same-sex couples due to the state's Religious Freedom Restoration Act. While critics called for boycotts, claiming the law enables discrimination, supporters rallied to the business with significant donations. The situation has placed the family-run restaurant at the center of a heated debate over religious freedom and LGBTQ+ rights.

To enforce a recent state-wide ban on beef, police in Malegaon, India, are requiring residents to submit "mugshots" and detailed physical descriptions of their cattle. Authorities believe that documenting unique features, such as tail length and coloring, will help them identify animals and prevent illegal cow slaughter.

The article explores the rare and miraculous instances of individuals surviving being lost at sea for extended periods without food or water. While such survival stories often seem like Hollywood fiction, they represent extraordinary feats of human endurance against impossible odds.

After a two-year shutdown, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has officially resumed operations at CERN. Following successful final tests, the world's largest particle accelerator has begun circulating beams through its 17-mile ring to restart physics experiments.

After a high-speed pursuit involving flying bullets and crashed vehicles, FBI agents captured 36-year-old Kevone Charleston in Forsyth County, Georgia, on Saturday morning. Charleston, who is suspected of involvement in 32 commercial robberies, was shot during the pursuit, which also resulted in injuries to two agents.

Sky watchers in western North America can witness a rare total lunar eclipse that is expected to last only four minutes and 43 seconds. According to NASA, this brief event will be the shortest total lunar eclipse of the century. While the best views are in the west, a partial eclipse will be visible across much of the nation.

The terrorist group Al-Shabaab has claimed responsibility for a deadly attack on Garissa University College in Kenya, leaving many dead and several others taken hostage. This incident marks a significant escalation in the group's cross-border activities and highlights the rapidly deteriorating security situation in East Africa.

Easter celebrates the Christian belief in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection, serving as a cornerstone of the faith. While the holiday focuses on salvation, it has also developed unique traditions like the Easter bunny and colorful eggs. Additionally, the date of the holiday shifts annually based on cosmic events, leading to coincidental alignments with lunar phenomena.

Despite years of claiming that athlete education is a core responsibility, the NCAA is now arguing in court that it has no legal obligation to ensure education is actually delivered. This shift in position comes in response to a lawsuit filed by former University of North Carolina athletes regarding a major academic fraud scandal.

A Connecticut juvenile court judge has denied a motion to release a 17-year-old girl from state custody, ruling that she must remain in temporary custody for the time being. Although the teen is currently in remission after undergoing chemotherapy for Hodgkin lymphoma, the judge also denied motions for visitation. Her attorneys argued that she should be allowed to return home because she is no longer at imminent risk of harm from her illness.

Mark Ronson's "Uptown Funk!" has become the longest-leading single of the 2010s after spending 13 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. This achievement marks only the 10th single in the chart's history to reach such a milestone. Additionally, newcomer Natalie La Rose broke into the top 10 with her debut single, "Somebody."

On March 24, Argentina's Esperanza Base recorded a temperature of 63.5 degrees Fahrenheit, which may be the highest ever measured in Antarctica. This record-breaking heat occurred on the Antarctic Peninsula and has prompted the World Meteorological Organization to form a committee of experts to investigate the event.

The United States is facing intense debate over state-level Religious Freedom Restoration Acts, particularly following controversy over a new law in Indiana. While these laws were designed to prevent the government from burdening religious practices, critics argue they are being used as a pretext to discriminate against the LGBTQ+ community.

Robert Lewis Burns Jr., the original drummer for the Southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd, died Friday night in a single-vehicle car crash in Cartersville, Georgia. The 64-year-old musician was not restrained at the time of the accident, which involved his car hitting a mailbox and a tree.

Kim Ki-Jong has been charged with attempted murder, assaulting a foreign envoy, and business obstruction following the stabbing of U.S. Ambassador Mark Lippert in Seoul. The attack occurred during a reunification event on March 5, resulting in facial injuries to the ambassador. Under South Korean law, Kim's trial is scheduled to begin within 14 days of his indictment.

In November, former British banker Rurik Jutting was charged with two counts of murder following a gruesome discovery at his Hong Kong apartment. A court hearing to determine if there was enough evidence to proceed to trial has been adjourned until May.

Thai Smile has unveiled a new Airbus A320 featuring a colorful "Adventure Time" livery to celebrate the hit Cartoon Network show. The aircraft's interior also incorporates the show's theme, with character designs featured on everything from headrests to air sickness bags.

Imprisoned soldier Chelsea Manning has joined Twitter to communicate with her followers using a voice phone to dictate messages. Because she lacks internet access in prison, a communications firm will post her tweets on her behalf.

The author argues that President Obama’s personal legacy is too deeply intertwined with reaching a nuclear deal with Iran, potentially clouding his diplomatic judgment. This political pressure has weakened America's negotiating position, making it appear as though the United States is more desperate for an agreement than Iran.

Universal's "Furious 7" is projected to have a massive weekend debut of up to $138 million, marking the largest North American opening since fall 2013. With a massive global release, the film could potentially cross $300 million in worldwide earnings by the end of Easter Sunday.

NFL legend Deion Sanders publicly called out his son, Deion Sanders Jr., on Twitter after the young athlete claimed he only eats "hood doughnuts." Reminding his son of his privileged lifestyle, the elder Sanders jokingly told him to "stop the hood stuff" by pointing to his trust fund and luxury assets.

An outside review by Columbia Journalism School professors concluded that *Rolling Stone* experienced an "institutional failure" regarding its flawed article about a purported gang rape at the University of Virginia. The review found that the failure spanned the entire editorial process, including reporting, editing, and fact-checking. In response, the magazine's managing editor issued an apology to those damaged by the story and its fallout.

The Shibuya ward in Tokyo has passed an ordinance to issue "partnership certificates" to same-sex couples, granting them certain rights held by married heterosexual partners. These certificates will allow partners to hold hospital visitation rights and co-sign tenancy agreements.

Blue Bell has temporarily shut down its Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, manufacturing plant following the discovery of listeria contamination in a serving of ice cream. Public health officials have warned consumers not to eat specific 3-ounce Blue Bell products originating from this plant, identified by certain letters following the coding date. This warning does not affect products made at other facilities.

In response to a query from lawmaker Antonio Inoki, Japanese Defense Minister Gen Nakatani informed parliament that the country's Air Self Defense Force has never encountered extraterrestrial UFOs. The statement clarifies that while the military monitors unidentified flying objects, they have never come across any objects from outer space.

Intense Saudi-led coalition airstrikes targeting strategic military sites in Sanaa have caused significant destruction to civilian infrastructure, including shattered homes and widespread power outages. While the Houthis maintain control of the capital, the fighting has resulted in hundreds of deaths and left residents fearing for their safety and access to essential services.

Film director David Lynch has announced he will no longer direct the revival of his influential cult series, *Twin Peaks*. He stated that the third season will proceed without him because the network did not provide enough funding to produce the show to his standards.

After a hot mic captured University of Kentucky guard Andrew Harrison using a racial slur to refer to Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky, Harrison issued a public apology for his "poor choice of words." He stated that the comment was made in jest and that he has already reached out to Kaminsky to express his respect and clarify his intentions.

The FBI has confirmed that high-profile Malaysian bomb maker Marwan, a key member of the terror group Jemaah Islamiyah, was killed during a January raid in the Philippines. Forensic DNA testing confirmed his identity, following initial suspicions raised by a severed finger found at the scene.

The EPA reported that a family of four from Delaware fell ill after being exposed to methyl bromide at a luxury villa in the U.S. Virgin Islands. Preliminary results confirmed the presence of the harmful pesticide in the rental unit, which can cause serious damage to the respiratory and central nervous systems.

Comedian Chris Rock is using social media to highlight racial disparities in policing through a series of tongue-in-cheek posts about being pulled over. By documenting his own traffic stops, Rock aims to capture the frustration and grief felt by many African Americans regarding the unequal treatment of Black citizens by law enforcement.

An explosion caused by an oil leak at a chemical plant in Fujian province, China, sparked a massive fire that injured six people. The blaze, which occurred at a facility producing carcinogenic paraxylene, was brought under control by more than 600 firefighters. While the explosion caused injuries from broken glass, local media has not reported any toxic chemical spills.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a 15-count indictment against FedEx, charging the courier service with various crimes including money laundering and violations of the Controlled Substances Act. The charges involve the illegal transportation of prescription pharmaceuticals, highlighting the legal ability to prosecute corporations as criminal entities.

Mark Wahlberg is set to star in and produce a new film titled "Patriots' Day," which depicts the Boston Marathon bombing and the subsequent manhunt. The film will be told from the perspective of former Boston Police Commissioner Ed Davis, with material researched by CBS News' "60 Minutes."

During a recent episode of "The Price Is Right," model Manuela Arbelaez accidentally revealed the correct price of a new car, much to the amusement of host Drew Carey. Although the mistake left Arbelaez mortified, the mishap was handled with humor and she later confirmed everything was fine.

Authorities have charged 32-year-old Carlos Colina following the discovery of human remains in a duffel bag in Cambridge, Massachusetts, over the weekend. Colina faces charges of assault and improper disposal of a body, while investigators continue to analyze evidence to determine if further charges are warranted.

Executive producer Brian Grazer announced that *Arrested Development* will return for a fifth season consisting of 17 episodes. While Netflix has not yet officially verified the news, the announcement promises more of the quirky comedy for the show's devoted fan base.

As the critically acclaimed series *Mad Men* approaches its series finale, the show marks the symbolic end of the 1960s era it has depicted for eight years. Despite not being a massive ratings hit, the show has become a cultural phenomenon, influencing fashion, lifestyle, and national conversation.

Many *Vampire Diaries* fans expressed frustration following Nina Dobrev's announcement that she will be leaving the CW series at the end of this season. In her farewell social media post, Dobrev reflected on her character's wild journey and stated that she always intended for Elena's story to span six seasons.

Four employees of a FabIndia store in Goa have been arrested after Federal Education Minister Smriti Irani discovered a surveillance camera pointed at the changing rooms. Following the minister's discovery, state authorities launched an investigation and confirmed the camera was capable of capturing footage of customers. While four staff members are in custody, the store manager remains at large.

Nine British citizens, including four children, were arrested by the Turkish military while attempting to cross illegally into Syria. While the specific motives for the group's travel remain unknown, the arrests occurred at the border amid the ongoing conflict in the region.

A Russian nuclear submarine caught fire while undergoing repairs at the Zvyozdochka shipyard in northwestern Russia. The fire was caused by welding work igniting the rubber insulation between the vessel's light and pressure hulls. Officials reported that the submarine was in dry dock and contained no ammunition at the time of the incident.

Beloved Turkish singer and songwriter Kayahan has passed away at the age of 66 following a long battle with cancer. The accomplished musician, who was a major influence on his generation, died in an Istanbul hospital five days after his birthday.

China's state prosecutors have formally charged former security czar Zhou Yongkang with bribery, abuse of power, and leaking state secrets. As a former member of the Politburo Standing Committee, Zhou becomes the highest-ranking official in the history of the Communist Party to face such corruption charges.

The provided text explores the tension between Jesus's teachings on the dangers of wealth and the practical necessity of financial support for his followers. It examines how the early apostles managed their livelihoods while adhering to a mission that often prioritized spiritual devotion over material security.

Three people were killed and five others were wounded when armed assailants stormed the attorney general's office in Afghanistan's Balkh province on Thursday. While most civilians and staff members have been rescued, an exchange of fire between security forces and the attackers is still ongoing.

In this op-ed, former Kentucky State Senator and trailblazer Bellovard criticizes Rand Paul’s presidential campaign announcement, arguing that his rhetoric contradicts his claims of "inclusion." She contends that his record of questioning landmark civil rights and voting rights legislation makes his message of expanding the Republican Party feel hollow and insincere.

The French-language network TV5Monde is gradually regaining control of its channels and social media accounts following an "extremely powerful" cyberattack. The network's websites and broadcasts were crippled after being hacked by an Islamist group, with ISIS logos appearing on their social media outlets.

After a flight from Abu Dhabi to New York, American traveler Jennifer Stewart discovered that Etihad Airways lost her most precious cargo: her two-year-old pet cat, Felix. The airline reported that the cat went missing on the grounds of JFK Airport shortly after the plane arrived.

Tuesday will see several high-profile legal and political events unfolding across the United States, including the conclusion of major trials in Massachusetts. Meanwhile, political developments include Senator Rand Paul's presidential announcement and a significant mayoral runoff in Chicago. Additionally, local elections in Ferguson will be heavily influenced by the ongoing fallout from the Michael Brown protests.

A massive four-alarm fire broke out Friday morning at the General Electric Appliance Park in Louisville, Kentucky, sending thick smoke over the surrounding area. While firefighters worked to contain the blaze, authorities reported that there were no injuries or trapped individuals. The cause of the fire remains unknown as emergency crews continue to manage the scene.

During his first campaign stop in Iowa, Senator Ted Cruz connected with voters through personal interactions and moments of shared prayer. Despite his aides' attempts to keep him on schedule, the candidate continued to engage with supporters to build religious and personal bonds.

Following a deadly terrorist attack at Garissa University College that killed 147 people, Kenyans have used the hashtag #147notjustanumber to honor the victims on social media. By sharing personal stories and photos, citizens are humanizing the casualties and highlighting the profound impact on their families.

The California Public Utilities Commission has ordered Pacific Gas & Electric to pay a record $1.6 billion penalty for unsafe gas system operations, including the 2010 San Bruno pipeline explosion. The majority of the fine is earmarked for mandatory spending on pipeline safety infrastructure and improvements. Commission President Michael Picker stated that the penalty follows PG&E's failure to uphold public trust and prevent the loss of life.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has been found guilty on all 30 counts related to the Boston Marathon bombing after an 11½-hour deliberation. The trial will now move into a penalty phase to determine whether the 21-year-old will face the death penalty. During this next stage, jurors will weigh the heinousness of the crimes against mitigating factors such as his age and mental health history.

A massive fire at the Abkatun Permanente oil platform off the coast of Mexico resulted in the deaths of four workers and injuries to 45 others. Authorities evacuated approximately 300 people from the site, and while the blaze was extinguished by Wednesday night, the cause of the fire remains unknown. Pemex has denied rumors of a platform collapse or an oil spill resulting from the incident.

The author notes that while Easter has historically resisted the commercialization seen during Christmas, many people—including Christians—remain largely unfamiliar with the significance of Holy Week. Given current cultural debates over identity and ethics, the author suggests that exploring the profound religious implications of this holiday is more important than ever.

Police in Lucknow, India, are deploying specialized drones equipped with cameras and pepper spray to manage violent protests and unruly crowds. While officials state the technology is a successful tool for crowd control, critics have raised concerns regarding the potential suppression of freedom of speech.

The Secret Service is facing a new scandal following allegations that supervisor Xavier Morales sexually assaulted a female employee. The victim claims that after making unwanted advances at a social event, Morales attempted to kiss her in the office and physically grabbed her when she resisted.

Investigators have finished collecting the primary evidence from the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site in the French Alps. While police have left the rugged terrain, a private security firm will remain to guard the area until the remaining debris is safely collected for further analysis.

While April 8, 2015, was a significant date for fans of the show *Lost*, it also marked "Rex Manning Day" in honor of the 1995 film *Empire Records*. Social media users celebrated the date by paying homage to the movie's fictional pop idol, a character played by Maxwell Caulfield.

Twisted Sister has announced that their 2016 "Forty and F*ck It" tour will be their final farewell to fans. The tour celebrates the band's 40th anniversary and features new drummer Mike Portnoy, who is stepping in following the death of A.J. Pero.

The critically panned film *Grace of Monaco*, starring Nicole Kidman, is set to premiere on Lifetime on May 25. Due to poor international performance, The Weinstein Co. decided to sell the film directly to the network rather than giving it a theatrical release in the U.S.

A massive tornado struck parts of Illinois on Thursday, causing significant damage in towns like Rochelle and Kirkland. While the storm caused one death in Fairdale, many areas are still struggling to assess injuries and damage due to thick debris blocking roads.

Eyewitness video showing Officer Michael Slager shooting unarmed Walter Scott has exposed discrepancies in the officer's initial reports regarding the fatal encounter. While Slager originally claimed he used a Taser during a struggle, the footage shows him shooting Scott eight times as the man ran away. As a result of the incident, Slager has been fired and charged with murder.

Kanye West has settled a civil lawsuit with photographer Daniel Ramos following a 2013 physical altercation at Los Angeles International Airport. The settlement comes just before the scheduled trial, resolving the legal battle over damages sought after West pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery.

Don McLean's handwritten manuscript for his legendary song "American Pie" was sold at Christie's for $1.2 million to an unnamed buyer. The 16-page document represents a piece of musical history that has remained a timeless cultural staple for over 44 years.

Despite serving seven years in prison for her 1996 affair with her 13-year-old student, Mary Kay Letourneau remains happily married to Vili Fualaau. The couple, who are now parents to two teenage daughters, will appear in an exclusive interview to celebrate their 10th wedding anniversary.

Don McLean's original manuscript for the song "American Pie" sold for $1.2 million at a Christie's auction on Tuesday. The singer decided to part with the manuscript to provide financial security for his family as he approaches his 70th birthday.

Mindy Kaling’s brother, Vijay Chokalingam, recently unveiled a new project that has drawn significant attention and criticism. Kaling jokingly remarked that the project brought "shame upon their family," highlighting the contrast between her successful sitcom and his new endeavor.

Actor John Travolta has expressed disapproval of the new HBO documentary "Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison of Belief," stating he has no interest in watching it. He defended his 40-year involvement with the Church of Scientology, noting that he has no desire to engage with such a negative portrayal of his experiences.

After spending nearly 30 years on Alabama's death row for crimes he did not commit, Anthony Ray Hinton was released from prison on Friday. Upon his freedom, Hinton expressed both gratitude and outrage, criticizing the legal system for failing to prevent his wrongful imprisonment.

Blues legend B.B. King was briefly hospitalized for dehydration caused by Type II diabetes but has since been released to rest at home. His daughter confirmed that he is feeling much better and is currently spending time with his grandchildren.

A newborn giraffe was born at the Dallas Zoo during a live-streamed event captured by ten cameras and broadcast by Animal Planet. Despite the intensity of the labor, the calf appeared to be in good condition, showing signs of strength by attempting to stand and nurse.

The Obama administration has indicated that there is no longer a specific timeframe for an Iraqi-led offensive to retake the strategic city of Mosul from ISIS. While previous plans suggested a spring invasion, officials now state that the operation could happen soon or may be delayed indefinitely.

As the fourth season of *Game of Thrones* concludes, fans are preparing for a massive fifth-season premiere that will air simultaneously in 170 countries. Expert Doug Gross suggests that viewers can expect major story arcs to begin converging as the series progresses.

Popular Chinese TV host Bi Fujian is facing controversy after being filmed using profanity to criticize the late Chairman Mao Zedong during a dinner party. Although the guests laughed at his improvised lyrics, Bi has since issued a public apology for the "grave social consequences" caused by his remarks.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has been found guilty on all 30 counts related to the 2013 Boston Marathon bombings. For survivors like Rebekah Gregory, the verdict brings a sense of legal closure but fails to fully compensate for the profound physical and emotional pain caused by the attacks.

Emmy-winning actor Richard Dysart has died at the age of 86 following a long illness. He was best known for his role as the cranky senior partner Leland McKenzie on the long-running NBC drama *L.A. Law*.

The author argues that President Obama is prematurely relinquishing the economic leverage provided by congressional sanctions that forced Iran to the negotiating table. The article warns that by easing these pressures, the administration risks losing its ability to prevent Iran from developing nuclear capabilities.

The VII Summit of the Americas in Panama City shifted from a symbolic focus on U.S.-Cuba relations to a "triangle of tension" due to the inclusion of Venezuela. While the summit was intended to celebrate the thawing of ties between President Obama and President Castro, political friction between various heads of state threatened the event's diplomatic goals.

Democratic presidential hopefuls Martin O'Malley and Jim Webb recently shared a stage at an awards dinner in Iowa, highlighting their vastly different political styles. While O'Malley is a former governor comfortable with hands-on retail politics, Webb is a decorated veteran who maintains a more stoic and reserved demeanor.

The Taliban has released an 11-page biography of founder Mullah Mohammed Omar to commemorate the 19th anniversary of his leadership. The document serves to assert that Omar remains the leader of the group and aims to dispel growing rumors regarding his death.

A viral photo of a cat on a staircase has sparked a massive social media debate over whether the animal is moving up or down the steps. Much like the famous "The Dress" optical illusion, the image has divided users as they argue over the construction of the stairs and the direction of the cat's motion.

Several storms triggered tornado sirens across Kansas on Wednesday night, with sightings reported near Goddard and southwestern Kansas. Experts warned that these nighttime tornadoes pose a significant danger to communities as storms continue to develop.

After losing his 25-year-old brother to cancer, a grieving man sought comfort by calling a local Catholic church to speak with a priest. However, he was turned away by a staff member because he was not a member of that specific parish. This experience left him feeling rejected during his moment of greatest need, contributing to his decision to stop praying.

Liana Barrientos is facing criminal charges after it was discovered that she married multiple men in New York without divorcing her previous husbands. Now 39, she faces counts of offering false instruments for filing due to lying on a 2010 marriage license application.

Two connected shootings in the Washington area left a security guard in critical condition after a domestic kidnapping incident began at the U.S. Census Bureau headquarters. The suspect's vehicle was spotted at the facility, where a guard was shot while approaching the vehicle during an argument between two individuals.

An Amnesty International report is calling for urgent action to address the increasing attacks and persecution of women's rights activists in Afghanistan. The report highlights how activists face threats from the Taliban, warlords, and government officials alike. This publication follows the international outcry over the brutal murder of Farkhunda, a young woman whose death underscored the growing dangers faced by women in the region.

The University of Michigan has decided to proceed with a screening of "American Sniper" despite a petition from over 200 students protesting the film. While some students argued the movie's depiction of the Iraq War could negatively impact the local Arab-American community, the university moved forward with the event as part of its UMix series.

Former Satyam Computers chairman Ramalinga Raju and nine others have been sentenced to seven years in prison for their roles in a massive $1.6 billion corporate fraud. The case stems from a 2009 scandal where Raju admitted to inflating profits through fictitious assets and nonexistent cash.

Carlos Colina, 32, has been charged with murder following the discovery of human remains in a duffel bag in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He is scheduled to be arraigned on the murder charge on April 14, after previously facing charges for assault and improper disposal of a body.

The first six "Star Wars" films are being released on digital HD, featuring special behind-the-scenes content for fans. A highlight of these features includes sound designer Ben Burtt explaining how various animals were used to create the unique sounds of the Geonosians.

An Iranian military aircraft performed an unsafe maneuver by flying within 50 yards of a U.S. Navy helicopter over the Persian Gulf. U.S. officials are concerned that the incident may have been ordered by local commanders rather than top leadership, potentially signaling a lack of control over regional forces.

Photographer Johan Bavman documented the experiences of Swedish fathers to explore the nation's generous parental leave policies. Sweden provides a total of 480 days of leave, with 390 days being partially paid to allow parents to focus on newborn care.

A judge has ruled that Craig Hicks, who is charged with the murders of three Muslim college students in Chapel Hill, is eligible for the death penalty. Hicks was arrested in February after shooting the victims, who were his neighbors, in the head.

HBO has released a teaser for the second season of *True Detective*, which is set to premiere on June 21. The new season stars Colin Farrell, Vince Vaughn, Rachel McAdams, and Taylor Kitsch in a story involving a bizarre murder and a web of conspiracy in California.

Lauren Hill, the 19-year-old basketball player known for her inspirational fight against brain cancer, has died. Her story gained worldwide attention last year when she fulfilled her dream of playing college basketball through a special NCAA accommodation.

Indiana Pacers player Chris Copeland was stabbed early Wednesday morning outside a New York City nightclub. While two Atlanta Hawks players were arrested following the incident, police stated they were not involved in the stabbing itself but faced charges for obstruction.

During a visit to Iowa, former Maryland Governor Martin O'Malley challenged the notion that Hillary Clinton is the "inevitable" Democratic presidential frontrunner. He noted that history is full of examples where frontrunners lost their perceived inevitability, drawing a parallel to Clinton's own experience in 2008.

Hip-hop artist Nelly was arrested in Tennessee on felony drug possession charges after a state trooper pulled over his private bus for missing regulatory stickers. The stop, which occurred on Interstate 40, led to charges including possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia.

Hundreds of mourners gathered in Summerville, South Carolina, to celebrate the life of Walter Scott, a U.S. Coast Guard veteran fatally shot by a police officer. The service honored Scott as a catalyst for social change while his family and friends gathered to honor his memory.

After enduring 12 years of severe domestic abuse in rural Guatemala, Adelma Cifuentes narrowly survived an attempted murder ordered by her husband. Despite her sons' efforts to save her, the attack resulted in the loss of her arm and highlighted the lack of support within her conservative community.

Hillary Clinton has officially announced her candidacy for the 2016 presidential election, a move expected to boost her sagging poll numbers. As one of the strongest candidates in decades, she brings extensive political experience and a seasoned ability to navigate modern media and partisan conflicts.

Ryan Gosling's directorial debut, *Lost River*, has remained a highly divisive film since its premiere, facing both mockery and critical debate. However, the film has been widely praised for its portrayal of a decaying Detroit, which serves as the essential backdrop for its post-industrial gothic story. Gosling noted that the city's crumbling architecture was the central inspiration and necessary foundation for the entire project.

To kick off peak season, 7-Eleven is hosting its first "Bring-Your-Own-Cup" Slurpee Day this Saturday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Customers can fill any sanitary, creative vessel—such as trophies or sand buckets—for the price of a medium Slurpee. To ensure practicality, any brought items must fit through a 10-inch-diameter hole in the in-store displays.

Elizabeth Sedway was removed from an Alaska Airlines flight in Hawaii after she claimed she could not fly without a doctor's note due to cancer. Although the incident caused significant delay and frustration, she eventually made it home to California and received an apology from the airline.

The University of Virginia is facing an investigation into its history of handling sexual assault allegations, specifically regarding its failure to expel students even when they admitted to misconduct. This inquiry includes an examination of how officials managed the allegations presented in a discredited *Rolling Stone* article.

Following months of protests and civil rights investigations, the Department of Justice is set to begin negotiations with Ferguson to restructure its police department due to patterns of racial discrimination. This shift comes amid significant local activism and recent election results that have brought new leadership to the city council.

A high-speed driving experience at Walt Disney World Speedway turned fatal on Sunday when a Lamborghini crashed into a guardrail. The passenger, 36-year-old Gary Terry, died at the scene, while the 24-year-old driver was hospitalized with minor injuries.

During an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta, a passenger named Oliver Minatel was attacked by a stranger using a cord while he was sleeping. The incident occurred during the flight's descent, prompting other passengers to intervene and help Minatel.

Millionaire real estate heir Robert Durst has been charged with unlawful possession of a firearm after authorities allegedly found a revolver in his hotel room. This indictment follows recent legal developments in his first-degree murder case, where he is accused of killing his friend Susan Berman.

Nearly 100-year-old graffiti left by World War I soldiers has been discovered in an underground chalk quarry near Naours, France. The inscriptions, which include names and home addresses, serve as a stark historical record of the soldiers who once occupied the site.

President Obama's historic nomination of Loretta Lynch to become the first African-American woman attorney general is facing an unprecedented delay in the Senate. The wait for her confirmation vote has now lasted longer than the combined waiting periods of the previous eight nominees.

NASA scientists recently outlined concrete steps for discovering extraterrestrial life over the next two decades, building on the progress made since the discovery of the first sun-like star planet 20 years ago. With nearly 2,000 confirmed exoplanets discovered through ground-based surveys and the Kepler satellite, researchers are increasingly focused on identifying rocky, Earth-like planets among thousands of candidates.

After months of presenting 131 witnesses, the defense for former NFL star Aaron Hernandez has rested its case in less than a day. Hernandez is on trial for the 2013 shooting death of Odin Lloyd, a case built largely on circumstantial evidence. The trial now moves toward closing arguments and jury deliberations.

During the 2015 Masters "Moving Day," Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods both finished their rounds at six under par, showing flashes of brilliance but failing to secure a definitive lead. While McIlroy briefly threatened to take control, late mistakes kept him from pulling away, and Woods showed signs of his former class despite his unpredictable current form.

A Delaware family is recovering from a sudden illness in the U.S. Virgin Islands that federal officials suspect may have been caused by pesticide exposure. While the father is in stable condition, his two teenage sons remain in critical condition following the incident at their rental villa.

A New York judge recently authorized the service of divorce papers via Facebook to ensure a defendant was officially notified of a lawsuit. This ruling addresses the common challenge of "service of process," where individuals often evade process servers to delay legal proceedings.

UNRWA Commissioner-General Pierre Krähenbühl is making an emergency visit to the Yarmouk refugee camp in Syria to assess the dire humanitarian situation. The visit aims to address the safety of 18,000 residents, including thousands of children, who remain threatened by ongoing conflict and armed group control.

In a daring heist reminiscent of a Hollywood movie, a gang of thieves bypassed modern cybercrime trends to rob a London vault using old-fashioned methods. The criminals accessed the jewelry district vault by descending an elevator shaft, executing a sophisticated raid that hasn't been seen in the city for decades.

The release of *Furious 7* earned a record-breaking $146 million over its opening weekend, but many viewers found the experience deeply emotional due to the late Paul Walker's involvement. Fans took to social media to praise the film's tribute to the actor, whose scenes were completed using body doubles and CGI after his death in 2013.

To honor her legacy 20 years after her death, Selena's family is working with a tech company to create a "digital embodiment" of the singer using hologram-like technology. The project aims to allow new generations of fans to experience her persona through a lifelike, interactive digital version of the star.

A gastrointestinal outbreak has affected 100 people, including passengers and crew, aboard the cruise ship *Celebrity Infinity*. The CDC is investigating the cause of the illness and has scheduled staff to meet the ship in San Diego to manage the situation. In response, Celebrity Cruises has implemented increased cleaning and disinfection procedures to contain the outbreak.

The original cast of *Twin Peaks* has released a video supporting David Lynch in his salary dispute with Showtime, which led to his departure from the show's revival. Using the hashtag #SaveTwinPeaks, actors like Sherilyn Fenn and Sheryl Lee expressed that continuing the project without Lynch would be incomplete.

A former TSA agent was sentenced to six months in jail after pleading guilty to charges involving the secret filming of a female co-worker. Investigators discovered that the man had also broken into the victim's home to capture over 1,500 photos and 90 videos of her.

Five young Chinese feminists face up to five years in prison after being detained for their gender equality activism. Prosecutors are currently deciding whether to move forward with charges of "disturbing public order" following an international outcry over their arrests.

A 20-to-30-foot section of a fiberglass boat, suspected to be debris from the 2011 Japanese tsunami, was recently discovered and towed to the coast of Oregon. Upon inspection, biologists found several specimens of yellowtail jack fish inside the fragment, which are species typically found in Japanese waters. This discovery suggests the debris traveled over 4,000 miles across the Pacific Ocean.

Two Troy University students, Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee, have been arrested and charged with multiple sexual battery offenses following a spring break incident in Panama City Beach. The investigation began after police discovered video footage of the assault while investigating an unrelated shooting.

This week's trending stories include the surprise announcement that the entire "Star Wars" saga will be released on digital HD. Additionally, Mindy Kaling's brother made headlines by claiming he faked his racial identity to gain admission to medical school.

ISIS claimed to have seized control of parts of Iraq's largest oil refinery following a Saturday assault, releasing images of the takeover. However, Iraqi government officials denied these claims, insisting that security forces maintain full control of the strategic facility.

For the first time since 1962, the United States has allowed Cuba to participate in the Summit of the Americas, marking a significant shift in regional diplomacy. As the summit begins in Panama, all eyes are on how the two nations will interact alongside other key players like Venezuela. Cuba aims to use the event to re-establish its international presence and influence within the region.

An Alaska Airlines flight returning to Seattle after reporting unusual banging in its cargo hold discovered a stowaway inside. The individual was identified as a Menzies Aviation ramp agent who had accidentally fallen asleep in the cargo hold during the flight. Authorities confirmed that the man was not in any danger and the incident was resolved safely.

One year after the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls by jihadists in Nigeria, the world continues to reflect on the horrific crime. President-elect Muhammadu Buhari marked the anniversary by expressing his sympathy for the victims and their families while acknowledging the global outrage caused by the abduction.

Following the fatal shooting of Walter Scott by a white police officer, artist Phillip Hyman created a hooded angel with black wings near the scene. The sculpture has since become a powerful icon for the Black Lives Matter movement and was featured prominently at local protests.

A 21-year-old man with cerebral palsy was left alone in a Philadelphia park for four days with only a blanket and a Bible. Police say his mother abandoned him on Monday morning to travel to Maryland to visit a boyfriend. The mother now faces multiple charges following the discovery of her son in the woods.

After his tech startup failed to secure investment, entrepreneur Jia Jiang launched the "100 Days of Rejection" project to confront his fear of failure head-on. This series of social challenges inspired his new book, *Rejection Proof*, which blends autobiography with motivational advice.

While traveling to an interview in Washington, D.C., a CNN crew encountered a mother duck and her brood of ducklings attempting to cross a busy street. Pedestrians and restaurant patrons worked together to corral the ducklings and used an umbrella to guide them safely across the road.

Police have added attempted murder to the charges against Nyia Parler, who is accused of leaving her quadriplegic son in the woods for several days. Parler will face multiple charges, including aggravated assault, once she completes a required treatment program in Maryland to allow for her extradition to Philadelphia.

The United States is lodging a formal complaint against Russia following an "unsafe and unprofessional" interception of a U.S. reconnaissance plane over the Baltic Sea. While the Pentagon described the Russian pilot's maneuvers as aggressive, Russian state media claimed the U.S. aircraft was flying toward their border with its transponder turned off.

Nyia Parler was taken into custody in Maryland after Philadelphia police reported she left her 21-year-old quadriplegic son alone in the woods to visit a boyfriend. While she faces charges in Philadelphia, Maryland police stated she cannot be extradited until she completes an unspecified medical treatment.

Kansas Governor Sam Brownback has signed a first-of-its-kind law banning the "dismemberment abortion" procedure commonly used during the second trimester. While supporters view the measure as a groundbreaking step, opponents warn that it is one of the most restrictive abortion laws in the country.

Jill Duggar Dillard, the first daughter from the reality show *19 Kids and Counting* to marry, has given birth to her first child, a son named Israel David. The 9-pound baby arrived over a week past his due date, following the expectations of his mother, who is a student midwife.

Authorities are investigating the killing of longtime Wayne Community College employee Ron Lane as a potential hate crime. The suspect, Kenneth Morgan Stancil III, was a former work-study student who worked alongside Lane in the school's print shop.

Legendary Australian cricket captain and broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at the age of 84. Renowned as both a record-breaking leg-spinner and a world-famous commentator, he was widely considered one of the most iconic figures in the history of the sport.

Irish betting company Paddy Power has deleted a controversial tweet comparing Newcastle United's football losses to the killing of unarmed African-American men. The company issued an apology following backlash, claiming the post was intended as a joke.

Migrants from Africa and the Middle East continue to arrive in Europe in large numbers, with nearly 1,000 people rescued off the coast of Libya this past Friday. This surge follows a significant increase in arrivals during the first months of 2015, with many travelers using Libya as a transit point.

President Barack Obama stated he is fully committed to ensuring Israel maintains a military advantage over Iran following the recent nuclear deal. While acknowledging Prime Minister Netanyahu's concerns regarding the agreement, Obama emphasized that the U.S. will work to protect Israel's security.

The Cape Verde Islands possess a deep-rooted cultural connection to music, fueled by a history as a diverse melting pot of races and traditions. This unique blend of influences, shaped by its history as a crossroads for various groups, has produced the country's distinct musical identity.

New research suggests that the play "Double Falsehood," previously attributed to Lewis Theobald, was actually written by William Shakespeare and John Fletcher. Using computer software to analyze linguistic patterns, scholars found a "landslide" match between the play and Shakespeare's known works. This discovery could potentially add a significant new work to Shakespeare's historical literary canon.

Following a massacre at a university in Garissa that killed 147 people, the Kenyan government has frozen 86 bank accounts linked to suspected Al-Shabaab supporters. Officials stated that they are continuing to track the finances of those suspected of ties to the militant group as they work to prevent further terror-related funding.

Jodi Arias was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for the 2008 murder of her ex-boyfriend, Travis Alexander. Before her sentencing, Arias expressed remorse for her actions, while the victim's family provided impact statements to the court.

Chinese authorities have formally detained activist Wu Rongrong and four others for planning to protest against sexual harassment on International Women's Day. The activists face a legal deadline on April 13, at which point they must either be released or formally arrested, a process that typically results in conviction.

In honor of her activism for girls' education, NASA astrophysicist Amy Mainzer has named an asteroid after Nobel Peace Prize winner Malala Yousafzai. The decision was made to immortalize the activist's story and her resilience following her life-saving recovery from a targeted attack.

Emy Afalava, a decorated veteran born in American Samoa, is fighting for the right to vote after being denied citizenship by the federal government. Despite being born on U.S. soil and subject to American law, he faces legal hurdles that prevent him from exercising the rights guaranteed by the Fourteenth Amendment.

The recent Ebola epidemic has infected over 25,000 people and resulted in more than 10,000 deaths, leaving survivors with life-altering consequences. While the crisis has stabilized compared to dire initial predictions, it has exposed significant flaws in global government systems and public health protections. Although the peak of the outbreak has passed, new infections continue to occur weekly.

Attorney General Eric Holder issued a memo to all U.S. Justice Department personnel strictly prohibiting the solicitation of prostitution, regardless of whether the practice is legal in a specific jurisdiction. Holder argued that such solicitation fuels the demand for human trafficking, thereby increasing the exploitation of both minors and adults.

Nashville's district attorney has banned prosecutors from offering female sterilization as an option in plea deals following public outrage over the practice. Critics argue that offering such deals evokes a dark history of forced sterilization and eugenics used against marginalized groups. While the practice has occurred multiple times in the past five years, the ban aims to prevent these controversial deals from continuing.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has been found guilty on all counts for his role in the Boston Marathon bombing. While the verdict was expected, the event has sparked debate over how to prevent similar violence from young men in the future. Some observers express concern that growing global Muslim populations will lead to more such attacks, though the article suggests this fear is based on specific beliefs.

The video of white police officer Michael Slager killing unarmed black man Walter Scott has sparked national outrage and led to Slager's arrest for murder. While the footage provided accountability, the incident raises troubling questions about how many similar incidents go unrecorded and unpunished. This event highlights the ongoing debate regarding police conduct and the necessity of third-party documentation in law enforcement encounters.

Apple has released a new mobile operating system update featuring a more diverse range of emojis representing various races, ethnicities, and sexual orientations. While the update has drawn both praise and criticism, many see the new images as vital symbols of mainstream recognition for underrepresented groups.

With Hillary Clinton officially announcing her 2016 presidential candidacy, she becomes the primary barometer for gender equality in the United States. Her campaign carries a unique burden, as a victory would represent a historic step for women's political inclusion, while a loss could lead to a false sense of complacency regarding gender progress.

NBC is debuting the miniseries "A.D. The Bible Continues," a sequel to the hit History Channel series that follows the early days of Christianity after Jesus' resurrection. The 12-week series stars Juan Pablo Di Pace and Greta Scacchi and serves as one of several highly anticipated shows premiering this week.

The Pentagon has released a map showing that coalition forces have reclaimed 25-30% of the Iraqi territory previously seized by ISIS. While these gains in central and northern Iraq represent significant progress, officials warn that the conflict remains dynamic and battle lines may fluctuate.

Arsenal kept their Premier League title hopes alive with a 1-0 victory over Burnley, thanks to a first-half goal from Aaron Ramsey. The win moves the club within four points of first-place Chelsea heading into their upcoming head-to-head matchup.

The author expresses profound distress over bystander video showing Officer Michael Slager shooting Walter Scott as he fled and subsequently planting an item by his body. While acknowledging the importance of the presumption of innocence, the author argues that the video provides undeniable evidence that challenges Slager's self-defense claims.

Drawing on a psychological study where patients with happy endings had more positive memories of unpleasant procedures, the author argues that the way an experience ends shapes our overall recollection. This principle is being applied to the American tax system, suggesting that the final outcome of the tax process heavily influences how citizens perceive the entire experience.

The Yarmouk refugee camp near Damascus has become a symbol of the devastating scale of the Syrian civil war following a recent takeover by ISIS fighters. In response to the takeover, the Syrian government has launched a heavy bombing campaign that has further leveled the area and caused constant loss of life.

The 2015 MTV Movie Awards featured a mix of viral highlights and comedic misfires, ranging from Channing Tatum’s dance moves to Amy Schumer’s provocative opening monologue. While some segments like Schumer's jokes were praised for being inventive, other moments like her archery fail were noted as misses.

Marvel Studios has released a new poster revealing Paul Bettany's portrayal of the Vision, ending speculation about the character's appearance in *Avengers: Age of Ultron*. This official reveal provides fans with their first full look at the heroic android before the film's release next month.

After more than two years of legal proceedings, Aaron Hernandez was sentenced to life in prison for the first-degree murder of Odin Lloyd. During the sentencing, Lloyd's mother, Ursula Ward, delivered an emotional tribute to her son, describing him as the backbone of their family.
